newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fundamentals key for crown longterm - Sweden FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Fundamentals key for crown longterm - Sweden FinMin.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday that economic fundamentals were the key issue for currency development in the longterm.
Repeating earlier comments that he was not particularly worried about the crown's weakness, Asbrink said fundamentals were continuing to head in the right direction.
Inflation was low, and both the current account and public finances were strong.

"This is the development in fundamentals. This will also come through, has come through and will continue to come through when we look at foreign exchange or bond market developments," Asbrink told a press briefing.
Asbrink said he expected to see fluctuations in the currency and even in the bond market.
"I am not especially worried," he said.
The Swedish crown hit its lowest point for a year on Friday, but Asbrink said then that he did not have any great worries about the crown.
"A slow crown softening has been going on since the autumn of 1996. With an inflation target and a floating crown this is something you have to be prepared for," he said.

The currency slid to 4.5274 per mark in early trade on Friday, from 4.5015 on Thursday and later fell further to 4.5710, its lowest level in 12 months, breaking one technical support level after another on its way.
On Monday at 1250 GMT it was trading at 4.5800.
